payload.headline: Microsoft slips 1.25% to 489.93 on reported outage; support holds, hold stays

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and profit margins are still improving, but free cash flow is shrinking and the price needs much faster cash growth than the business shows, so the case for holding rests on that spending paying back.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only near the bottom of the own-history fair range. Swing: the existing trade stays on, and new entries go in at the top of the first support zone.
summary.act_at: Add at 474.82; swing entry at 485.06, stop 475.34, target 503.99

payload.happening: Microsoft fell 1.25% to 489.93. That puts it back inside the 485.58–490.27 zone where it has been trading and just above the 475.34–485.06 support zone. The Verge reported that Microsoft declared a 'Code Red' after a large Outlook outage. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27, and analysts' earnings estimates have risen 2.19% over the last 30 days.
payload.business: The core business is still improving. Sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, faster than the 18.3% two quarters ago. Trailing revenue is 346.4B, up from 293.8B. The operating margin, the share of each sales dollar left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. The weak spot is cash. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and the free-cash-flow margin is only 17.31%. The filings note that each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, compared with 51¢ three years ago. In plain words, heavy spending is not paying back yet. That spending is what puts the cash and the valuation at risk. The reported Outlook outage mainly hurts sentiment and reputation. It would only become a business problem if customers left over it, and nothing in the data shows that (general knowledge). Things not at risk today: the balance sheet holds 29.0B in net cash with 64.5B of liquidity, and share count fell 0.27% over the year, so owners are not being diluted.

worth.text: There are two ways to value Microsoft here, and they disagree sharply. The cash-flow method (a discounted cash flow, or DCF: future cash brought back to today's money at a 9.9% discount rate) starts from today's 60.0B of free cash flow. It gives 183.71 in the bear case, 222.45 in the base case and 295.41 in the bull case. Working backwards, today's price only makes sense if free cash flow starts growing at about 39.3% a year. Even 30% starting growth gives a value of just 350.1. The other method compares the stock with its own past price-to-sales ratios (share price compared with sales per share). That gives 474.82 at the low end, 534.4 in the middle and 591.77 at the high end. The price of 489.93 sits near the bottom of that range. Against similar companies the stock looks expensive: it trades at 10.5 times sales, while the peer median is 3.6. By earnings, the stock trades at 25.6 times trailing earnings and 20.2 times next year's estimate. The gap between the two methods comes down to one assumption: whether today's lower cash flow is temporary. Two of the three measures lean expensive. I use the own-history range because it treats today's depressed cash flow as temporary, but that is a choice, not a fact.
worth.key_assumption: The spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so the stock's own sales-multiple history is a fair guide and today's cash flow is not.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 18.8% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, compared with 18.3% two quarters ago.
Profitability is rising: the operating margin is 47.1%, up from 46.27%, and next-year earnings estimates rose 2.2% in 30 days to 24.2.
The price of 489.93 is near the bottom of the stock's own-history fair range (474.82–591.77), and the balance sheet has 29.0B of net cash.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, compared with 51¢ three years ago.
Today's price assumes free cash flow starts growing at about 39.3% a year. The base cash-flow value is only 222.45.
The stock costs 10.5 times sales, while the peer median is 3.6. It also trades below its 20-day average (516.38, falling) and its 50-day average (518.64).

levels.what: Today's close sits inside the 474.82–534.4 fair range. Nothing here calls for selling, and it is not cheap enough to add.
The bottom of the own-history fair range, just below the 475.34–485.06 support zone. This is the add level.
The bottom of the lower support zone (464.55–471.29). A close below it breaks both support zones and the fair range. In that case, no new adds until the 2027-01-27 report.

longterm.why: Sales growth, margins and estimates are improving, but free cash flow is shrinking and two of three valuation measures lean expensive. Hold, and add only at 474.82.

swing.why: The existing trade is still on: the close of 489.93 held above its 475.34 stop. New entries go in at 485.06, the top of the support zone, rather than chasing the price. The stop is 475.34, and the target is 503.99, the bottom of the resistance zone. Price is below a falling 20-day average and the market is trading in a range, so the trade aims for the first resistance zone, not 511.78. Existing positions can still aim for 511.78.

decision.timing: Options expiring 2026-12-18 price a 7.1% move, so the swing target fits inside that window. Any swing position closes before the 2027-01-27 report, which options expiring 2027-02-19 price at a 13.7% move. Long-term money beyond the 474.82 add waits for that report's free-cash-flow figure.

change_mind: A close below 464.55 would break both support zones. The long-term action would turn to wait, with no adds until the 2027-01-27 report.

If the 2027-01-27 report shows trailing free cash flow still falling below 60.0B, the 'spending pays back' assumption weakens. The cash-flow values of 183.71–295.41 would then matter more than the own-history range.
A close above 523.42, the top of the upper resistance zone, would end the trading range. If that happens and the operating margin stays at or above 47.1%, the long-term view would move toward add.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: the long-term view stays hold and the swing trade stays on, because the close of 489.93 held above the 475.34 stop despite the reported Outlook outage. New swing entries move down to 485.06 and the target moves to 503.99, and the fair range now uses today's own-history values (474.82–534.4).
